newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Brunei's finance minister quits, sultan takes job.
newsitem.headline: Brunei's finance minister quits, sultan takes job.

text.p: Brunei's Finance Minister Jefri Bolkiah, who supervised an estimated $60 billion as chairman of the country's investment agency, has resigned, an official statement said on Wednesday.
His older brother, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, who is also prime minister and defence minister in the tiny oil kingdom on the fringes of a Borneo rainforest, will take over the job, the statement said.
"The prime minister has announced his majesty, the sultan, has accepted the resignation of his youngest brother Prince Jefri Bolkiah as the finance minister," the statement said.
"The prince has resigned from his post for personal reasons and on his own free will and will cease to be a member of the government of Brunei," it said.
Jefri was also chairman of the powerful Brunei Investment Agency, which controls an estimated $60 billion in overseas investments.
The announcement did not say whether Jefri would continue to hold that position, but sources close to the finance ministry said that was unlikely.
Jefri resigned as chairman of Royal Brunei Airlines six months ago.
The 40-year-old Jefri was appointed finance minister in 1986, two years after Brunei gained independence from Britain.

He has growing business interests both within Brunei and overseas, financial analysts said. He controls the lucrative mobile telephone service in Brunei through his family's investment in DST Communications Sdn bhd.

His family also controls a satellite television service in the country. His interests include hotels and the huge Jerudong amusement park outside the capital of Bandar Seri Begawan, whose facilities are free to the public.
The statement said the 50-year Sultan Hassanal had assumed responsibility for the finance ministry on February 23, Brunei's National Day.
That same day the sultan announced a five-year development plan of BR$7.2 billion, which aims to diversify the economy from its dependence on petroleum by boosting non-oil exports.
Jefri's resignation came amid renewed talk that the Brunei dollar could be delinked from the Singapore dollar in an effort to make the kingdom's non-oil exports more competitive.
Bruneian officials denied that sort of speculation when it first surfaced last July but have not been available for comment about the more recent talk.
